purpose: Curated catalog of AOP numbered trails being assembled for park use. AOP identifies trails by NUMBER on the map (green=Easy, blue=Moderate, black=Difficult); names here are observation-confirmed by the park team and also appear in onX. This is a working/authoring seed — it will be refined and is not final form. Not yet wired to map geometry (real per-trail centerlines are still owed; see brain/tasks/01_mvp/_done/community_trails_import.md). Sources retained per row so curation can keep or rewrite copy with provenance intact.
provenance_note: Descriptions for trails 1-11 are paraphrased from onX trail guides (onX-copyright — rewrite before public publish). Trail 96 is the park's own 2015 blog wording (via Wayback). Names confirmed against in-park observation by the park team (2026-05-29), so name provenance = observed, not onX-only.

trails.name: Launchpad
trails.description: Begins with a fine dirt-filled trail and a slight uphill climb. Once you reach Area 51, loose rock makes it feel like driving on a cobblestone road.

trails.name: Convergence
trails.description: Easy route that peels off Trail 1 (Launchpad) and curves toward the buggy side of the park. A convergence point for mountain runoff that feeds nearby Battle Creek.

trails.name: Major Tom
trails.description: A casual-side trail that is easy to underestimate; accessible, but complacency can catch out a starter vehicle or one with low ground clearance.

trails.name: Lifeform
trails.description: A peaceful uphill climbing connector with small rocks, exposed roots, and curving bends that bring you out to Trail 3.

trails.name: Descension
trails.description: A mild downhill that starts as a dirt flat and ends with a deeply rutted, eroded section; the lower rut also has an exposed tree root.

trails.name: Ascension
trails.description: A slippery slope when wet; when dry, a fun hill climb for all vehicle types.

trails.name: Little Dipper
trails.description: A full loop that connects back to itself and also feeds a few more difficult trails. Mostly flat throughout with little to no obstacles.

trails.name: Ground Control
trails.description: Like a child's roller coaster — slightly uphill then back down, over and over. Concentrated clusters of rock, but none are difficult to traverse.
A short loop with many rock and ledge obstacles that challenge drivers to negotiate angles and clearance. Passable by modified Jeeps and Trucks.
trails.note: Park's own 2015 description; the park referred to it by number only.

coverage.backbone_note: The remaining ~110 numbered trails carry only a number + difficulty color on the map. They get added to this catalog as field observation, onX, or park-supplied names land. No fabricated entries.
